sections.heading: Commercial Glazing Leeds: 5 Powerful Proven Strategies to Control Cost, Compliance and Heat Loss in Office Refurbishment
body: ONLINE DESIGNER

Commercial glazing Leeds refurbishment projects are increasingly shaped by three pressures: rising energy costs, tighter compliance requirements and the need for programme certainty in live environments.

Across Leeds city centre and the wider West Yorkshire region, ageing office stock is being upgraded rather than rebuilt. For Estimators, Quantity Surveyors and Project Managers, commercial glazing is no longer simply a façade decision. It is a cost-control and risk-management package that must integrate cleanly into wider refurbishment works.
Fenster fitted the aluminium windows at Headrow Court on The Headrow in Leeds, a conversion of four former office buildings into 108 student studios, completed in October 2025.

sections.heading: 1. Start with Measurable Heat Loss, Not Assumptions
body: Many commercial buildings in Leeds were constructed before current thermal standards were introduced. Non-thermally broken frames and early-generation double glazing can significantly underperform compared to modern systems.
For QSs, the issue is not just comfort. It is operational expenditure. Heat loss increases demand on heating systems and affects long-term lifecycle modelling.
Before committing to office window replacement Leeds, a detailed survey should assess:
Frame condition and structural stability
Glazing unit performance
Air leakage around apertures
Integration with existing façade elements

At Headrow Court the aluminium windows were replaced across a converted building while improving the thermal envelope, working to a handover fixed by the academic year. The focus was on performance improvement grounded in accurate site data, not assumption.
Early diagnostics protect tender accuracy and reduce variation risk later in the programme.

sections.heading: 2. Evaluate Repair vs Replacement Through a Lifecycle Lens
body: A common tender-stage debate in commercial glazing Leeds projects is whether to repair or fully replace.

While targeted repairs may appear cost-effective initially, they can create repeat access costs and ongoing maintenance liabilities. Where frames lack thermal breaks or structural integrity, refurbishment often becomes reactive rather than strategic.
Office window replacement Leeds decisions should consider:
Capital cost versus long-term operational savings
Reduced maintenance cycles
Improved thermal performance
Risk of future remedial works
Aluminium windows Leeds commercial projects specify are often chosen because they provide predictable durability and extended service life.
For Estimators and QSs, lifecycle clarity reduces uncertainty. For Project Managers, it reduces the risk of phased rework disrupting future occupation.

sections.heading: 3. Specify Aluminium Systems That Support Buildability
body: Aluminium windows Leeds commercial refurbishment projects rely on offer structural strength, dimensional stability and compatibility with modern glazing units.
From a buildability perspective, this matters.

Precision manufacturing reduces tolerance-related issues during installation. At Headrow Court the aluminium systems were selected to suit a converted facade while delivering improved thermal performance.
Modern aluminium glazing systems support:
Improved U-values aligned with Part L requirements
Structural integrity for larger openings
Compatibility with acoustic glazing where required
Long-term durability with minimal maintenance
For city centre commercial glazing Leeds projects, where access and sequencing are tightly controlled, predictable installation methodology reduces programme risk.
Buildability is not just technical. It is commercial risk mitigation.

sections.heading: 4. Protect Programme Certainty in Live Leeds Environments
body: Many office window replacement Leeds projects occur in buildings that remain operational throughout works. City centre locations such as LS1 present access constraints, restricted working hours and coordination challenges with adjacent trades.
Programme control requires:
Clear phasing aligned to scaffold schedules
Coordination with roofing and façade packages
Controlled deliveries within constrained urban streets
Detailed RAMS tailored to site conditions
On Leeds city centre projects, glazing packages must integrate with the wider refurbishment sequence. Delays in commercial glazing can quickly affect internal fit-out or follow-on trades.
For Project Managers, disciplined sequencing and in-house installer management reduce uncertainty. For QSs, it protects programme-linked cost exposure.
Commercial glazing Leeds delivery should enhance, not complicate, the wider construction timeline.

sections.heading: 5. Align Compliance Early to Avoid Tender Drift
body: Part L compliance, safety glazing standards and acoustic requirements must be addressed at specification stage rather than post-contract.
Office window replacement Leeds projects frequently require:
Improved thermal performance
Safety glazing in designated areas
Acoustic mitigation in high-traffic zones
Early technical alignment reduces the risk of late-stage specification changes. It also prevents compliance-driven variation once installation has commenced.

Aluminium windows Leeds commercial projects adopt can be configured to meet regulatory performance requirements without extensive façade redesign, provided that compliance considerations are integrated from the outset.
For Estimators, this reduces ambiguity in tender submissions. For QSs, it supports tighter cost control. For Project Managers, it protects delivery timelines.

sections.heading: Commercial Glazing Leeds as a Structured Refurbishment Package
body: Commercial glazing Leeds refurbishment should be approached as a coordinated, performance-led package rather than an isolated installation trade.
Successful office window replacement Leeds programmes typically share common characteristics:
Early technical engagement
Accurate survey validation
Aluminium systems selected for durability and buildability
Compliance aligned pre-procurement
Programme sequencing integrated with wider works

The work at Headrow Court in Leeds shows how aluminium glazing can modernise an existing envelope on a building being converted to a new use. The focus was disciplined installation, measured thermal improvement and programme coordination, not exaggerated claims.

For Estimators, Quantity Surveyors and Project Managers operating across Leeds and West Yorkshire, commercial glazing is increasingly tied to cost certainty, compliance clarity and long-term asset performance.
When delivered with structured planning and honest specification, commercial glazing Leeds becomes a strategic investment that supports both financial control and building performance.

sections.heading: Commercial Glazing Replacement in London: Managing Cost, Compliance and Programme
body: ONLINE DESIGNER

sections.heading: Noticing the call for Commercial Glazing Replacement in London
body: Commercial glazing London projects rarely involve simple like-for-like upgrades. In a city defined by dense urban sites, live environments and complex planning constraints, commercial window replacement requires careful management of cost, compliance and programme sequencing.

Whether upgrading ageing office façades, replacing underperforming glazing in education buildings or modernising healthcare estates, commercial glazing replacement in London must be approached as a coordinated construction activity rather than a standalone trade.
Here we’ll outline key considerations shaping commercial glazing London projects and how structured delivery reduces risk across refurbishment schemes.

sections.heading: The Growing Demand for Commercial Glazing Replacement London
body: Across London, many commercial buildings constructed in the 1980s and 1990s are now reaching a performance tipping point. Outdated aluminium and steel systems often fail to meet modern thermal standards, acoustic requirements or safety expectations.
Commercial window replacement London schemes are typically driven by:
Poor thermal performance and rising energy costs
Failed sealed units and water ingress
Non-compliance with updated Building Regulations
Corporate ESG targets and EPC improvements
Tenant expectations for comfort and aesthetics

Glazing replacement is frequently one of the most visible and measurable improvements within a refurbishment programme. However, achieving those improvements without disrupting building operations requires structured planning.

sections.heading: Managing Cost in Commercial Glazing London Projects
body: Cost management within commercial glazing London schemes extends beyond material supply. It requires a clear understanding of lifecycle value, programme implications and specification accuracy.
Key cost drivers include:
Access requirements and scaffold sequencing
Façade interface complexity
Glazing specification (acoustic, solar control, toughened)
Phased installation in occupied buildings
Design revisions and late-stage variations
Early engagement significantly reduces financial risk. Reviewing drawings, structural tolerances and access constraints before installation begins helps prevent unforeseen site challenges.

In many commercial window replacement London projects, aluminium glazing systems offer strong lifecycle value. While initial specification may sit above basic alternatives, aluminium glazing London solutions provide long-term durability, reduced maintenance and improved thermal performance. Over time, this contributes to lower operational expenditure.
A well-planned glazing package protects both capital budget and long-term asset value.

sections.heading: Compliance in a London Refurbishment Environment
body: Commercial glazing London projects must align with stringent regulatory requirements. London’s regulatory scrutiny, particularly on larger public and mixed-use buildings, demands careful documentation and specification.
Core compliance considerations include:
Part L thermal performance requirements
Toughened or laminated safety glazing where required
Fire performance alignment where applicable
Acoustic performance in education and healthcare settings
Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS)
Site-specific health and safety inductions

Part L compliance plays a central role in commercial window replacement London schemes. Replacing outdated glazing with thermally broken aluminium systems and high-performance double glazing significantly improves U-values and reduces heat loss.

In sensitive environments such as schools and healthcare facilities, safeguarding and operational continuity must also be integrated into compliance planning. Glazing contractors must demonstrate structured documentation, safe working practices and controlled installer management.

sections.heading: Programme Coordination in Live Environments
body: London refurbishment projects often take place within fully operational buildings. Offices remain occupied. Schools continue term schedules. Healthcare facilities operate continuously.
Commercial glazing replacement therefore functions as a coordinated infrastructure upgrade within a live system.

A useful analogy is replacing structural components in an active transport network. If sequencing is poorly managed, disruption spreads quickly. When integrated correctly, improvements occur with minimal impact.
Effective programme management within commercial glazing London projects involves:
Phased installation aligned to access windows
Scaffold and mast climber coordination
Clear communication with site management
Controlled material delivery in constrained urban settings
Integration with roofing and façade packages
Aluminium glazing London systems are particularly suited to phased installation due to their structural stability and precision manufacturing tolerances.

sections.heading: Why Aluminium Glazing London Projects Favour Modern Systems
body: Aluminium glazing London solutions continue to be specified across commercial refurbishment projects due to their combination of structural performance and design flexibility.
Key advantages include:
Improved thermal performance through advanced thermal breaks
Structural integrity for larger glazed openings
Slim sightlines suitable for modern façade upgrades
Long service life with minimal maintenance
Compatibility with acoustic and solar-control glass

For commercial window replacement London schemes, aluminium systems offer adaptability. They can be integrated into existing structural openings or specified as part of broader façade redesign strategies.

In dense urban settings such as London, where façade performance directly impacts energy modelling and tenant expectations, aluminium glazing provides measurable performance improvements without compromising aesthetic quality.

sections.heading: Risk Mitigation Through Early Engagement
body: One of the most effective strategies in commercial glazing London projects is early-stage technical engagement.
Structural drawings
Façade interfaces
Access logistics
Scaffold sequencing
Programme milestones
Before installation begins, glazing contractors can identify risk areas and advise on realistic installation timelines.
This reduces:
Cost overruns
Design clashes

sections.heading: Delivering Commercial Glazing London with Control and Certainty
body: London’s commercial environment demands structured delivery, transparent compliance management and disciplined programme coordination.
Successful commercial glazing replacement projects in the capital are characterised by:
Clear specification alignment
Strong documentation and safety oversight
Controlled in-house installation teams
Early engagement with principal contractors
Lifecycle-focused cost planning
Commercial glazing London projects are not simply about replacing frames and glass. They are about enhancing asset performance while protecting programme integrity.

For asset managers, consultants and contractors operating within London’s complex construction landscape, structured commercial window replacement London solutions provide a route to measurable building improvements without introducing unnecessary risk.

sections.heading: Introduction
body: In healthcare construction, building performance directly impacts patient wellbeing, staff safety and operational efficiency. One often overlooked but critical element is the window, door and facade specification.
commercial window installation
. In hospitals, clinics and care environments, windows are not simply architectural features, they play a vital role in safety, infection control, comfort and long-term building performance.
This article explores how professional commercial window installation supports safer, more efficient healthcare facilities and why specialist contractors are essential in healthcare environments.

sections.heading: The Importance of Commercial Window Installation in Healthcare Construction
body: Healthcare buildings operate under unique conditions. They are high-occupancy, often operational 24 hours a day, and must meet strict regulatory and safety standards. Within this context, commercial window installation must be approached with care, expertise and an understanding of healthcare-specific requirements.
Correct installation ensures glazing systems perform as specified, supporting thermal efficiency, security and hygiene throughout the building’s lifecycle.

sections.heading: Enhancing Safety for Patients, Staff and Visitors
body: Safety is a core consideration in all healthcare construction projects. Professionally installed commercial windows contribute to safer environments through secure frames, appropriate glazing specifications and reliable locking mechanisms. Poor installation can lead to operational failures, safety risks and increased maintenance issues.
In facilities accommodating vulnerable patients, such as care homes and mental health units, secure glazing systems are particularly important in reducing risk while maintaining usability for staff.

sections.heading: Supporting Infection Control and Hygiene Standards
body: Infection control is a fundamental requirement in healthcare facilities. Commercial window installation plays an important role by ensuring units are properly sealed, easy to clean and resistant to moisture ingress. Gaps, poorly fitted frames or failing seals can compromise hygiene standards and create long-term maintenance challenges.
High-quality commercial glass installation supports effective cleaning regimes and helps healthcare providers maintain compliant, hygienic environments.

sections.heading: Improving Energy Efficiency and Environmental Stability
body: Healthcare buildings consume significant energy due to continuous operation. Commercial window installation directly affects thermal performance, helping to maintain stable internal temperatures and reduce heat loss.

Well-installed glazing systems support patient comfort, protect sensitive equipment and contribute to long-term energy efficiency. This is especially important in construction in healthcare facilities where operational costs must be carefully managed.

sections.heading: Acoustic Performance and Patient Privacy
body: Noise control is critical in healthcare environments, particularly in consultation rooms, wards and recovery areas. Commercial window installation influences acoustic performance by reducing external noise and limiting sound transfer between spaces.
Improved acoustic control supports patient privacy, enhances recovery conditions and creates calmer working environments for healthcare professionals.

sections.heading: Minimising Disruption in Live Healthcare Environments
body: Most healthcare construction services are delivered within live, operational buildings. Commercial window installation must therefore be carefully planned and phased to minimise disruption to patients and staff.

Experienced healthcare construction contractors coordinate closely with estates and facilities teams, managing access, noise and safety controls to ensure installations are completed efficiently without impacting day-to-day clinical operations.

sections.heading: Long-Term Efficiency Through Quality Installation
body: Correct commercial window installation reduces the likelihood of future issues such as failed units, drafts and reactive repairs. In healthcare environments, where downtime can have serious implications, long-term reliability is essential.
Investing in professional installation supports durability, reduces maintenance costs and ensures glazing systems continue to perform effectively over time.

sections.heading: Conclusion
body: Commercial window installation has a direct and lasting impact on safety, efficiency and comfort in healthcare facilities. From infection control and acoustic performance to energy efficiency and security, professionally installed glazing systems support the complex demands of healthcare construction.

sections.heading: Planned Maintenance and Lifecycle Performance of Commercial Windows and Doors in Healthcare Buildings

sections.heading: Introduction
body: In healthcare construction, responsibility does not end once installation is complete. Hospitals, clinics and care facilities rely on building components that perform consistently over long periods, often in demanding, high-use environments. Planned
commercial window maintenance
plays a vital role in ensuring safety, efficiency and compliance throughout the lifecycle of healthcare buildings.
This article explores why ongoing maintenance and lifecycle planning are essential for commercial windows in healthcare environments and how a proactive approach helps protect long-term investment.

sections.heading: Why Planned Maintenance Matters in Healthcare Facilities
body: Healthcare buildings operate continuously and are subject to higher levels of wear than many other commercial environments. Without planned maintenance, small issues such as worn hardware, failed seals or reduced thermal performance can escalate into safety concerns, operational disruption or increased costs.
In healthcare construction, planned maintenance supports reliability, reduces unexpected failures and helps facilities teams manage buildings more effectively.

sections.heading: Supporting Safety and Compliance Over Time
body: Commercial windows play an important role in safety, security and environmental control. Over time, hinges, locks and glazing units can degrade if not properly maintained. Planned maintenance ensures windows continue to operate safely, particularly in environments accommodating vulnerable patients.
Routine inspections and timely repairs help healthcare providers maintain compliance with internal safety policies and building regulations while reducing the risk of reactive call-outs.

sections.heading: Maintaining Energy Efficiency and Environmental Performance
body: Thermal performance can decline as glazing systems age. Failed seals, drafts or poorly functioning windows can impact internal temperatures and increase energy consumption. Planned commercial window maintenance helps identify these issues early, supporting stable internal environments and long-term energy efficiency.
In construction in healthcare facilities, maintaining consistent temperatures is essential for patient comfort, staff wellbeing and the protection of sensitive equipment.

sections.heading: Reducing Disruption in Live Healthcare Environments
body: Reactive repairs often require urgent access, which can be disruptive in busy healthcare settings. Planned maintenance allows work to be scheduled around operational needs, reducing disruption to patients, staff and visitors.
This proactive approach is particularly valuable in hospitals and care facilities where continuity of service is critical.

sections.heading: Extending the Lifecycle of Commercial Glazing Systems
body: Well-maintained commercial windows last longer and perform more reliably. Planned maintenance programmes can extend the service life of glazing systems by addressing minor issues before they develop into larger problems.
This supports better lifecycle performance, reduces the need for premature replacement and helps healthcare providers achieve better value from their original investment.

sections.heading: Responsive Repairs When Issues Arise
body: Even with planned maintenance in place, occasional faults can occur. Having access to reliable
commercial window repairs
ensures issues are resolved quickly and safely. Prompt repairs help maintain security, comfort and compliance while preventing further deterioration.
A structured maintenance and repair approach supports long-term building performance across healthcare estates.

sections.heading: A Responsible, Long-Term Approach to Healthcare Construction
body: Healthcare construction services extend beyond installation. A long-term view that includes maintenance, monitoring and aftercare is essential to ensure buildings remain safe and effective for years to come.

sections.heading: Conclusion
body: Planned commercial window maintenance plays a critical role in the long-term performance of healthcare buildings. By supporting safety, energy efficiency and operational continuity, proactive maintenance helps healthcare facilities operate reliably in demanding environments.
A structured, responsible approach to maintenance ensures commercial glazing systems continue to support the complex needs of healthcare construction long after installation is complete.

sections.heading: Condensation on New Windows: How Fenster Glazing Can Help
body: ONLINE DESIGNER
As the temperature drops and you cosy up your home during the colder seasons, you might have noticed condensation forming on the outside of your recently installed
double-glazed windows

Before you panic, let us assure you that this occurrence is not only normal but also indicative of your new glazing at work, showcasing its high energy efficiency. In this article, we delve into the reasons behind condensation on the exterior of your windows and explain why it’s a positive sign.

sections.heading: Why Does Condensation Appear Outside New Windows?
body: Many things can cause condensation on windows, such as using single-pane windows, insufficient weather sealing, or an energy-inefficient home. But the appearance of condensation on newly installed double-glazed windows can be confusing. Let’s take a closer look and explore why this happens.

The temperature difference between your home’s interior and exterior during the winter causes the water in the air to condense on cold surfaces. When you see condensation on the outside of your new windows, it signifies that your windows are diligently working to keep the cold air outside.

Instead of allowing precious heat to escape, they are preventing it from leaving, resulting in condensation forming on the external surface. While the sight of condensation may not look very nice, it serves as tangible evidence that your windows are of high quality and actively safeguarding your home’s comfort.

sections.heading: How Can Fenster Glazing Help?
body: , we specialise in providing double-glazed windows designed to offer numerous benefits, and one of these is the effective reduction of condensation. Here are just a few examples of the benefits our windows provide.

sections.heading: Continuously Sealed Windows
body: We work with marketing-leading manufacturers to ensure all our windows protect any home. Our windows are designed with bubble gaskets in their profiles, which are welded into the frame. These materials help create a continuous seal inside the windows to ensure they are weathertight. Therefore, our windows will keep your home at the perfect temperature, so the amount of condensation is minimised.

sections.heading: Double Glazing
body: All our windows also come with double glazing, which increases your home’s energy efficiency. Double glazing significantly retains the heat in the home and ensures no cold draughts get in. Not only does this help with condensation on the outside of your new windows, but it also keeps you at a comfortable temperature all year round. Another great benefit of this is that you will rely less on your heating, saving you money in the long run.

sections.heading: Fenster Glazing uPVC Windows
body: If you are concerned about condensation on or around your windows, speak to Fenster Glazing. Our team can explain what is normal, what needs checking and when replacement glass or improved ventilation may help. Call 01908 429200 or email info@fensterglazing.com.
or email us a

, and we will be happy to help.

sections.heading: Why You Should Consider Composite Doors For Your Home
body: ONLINE DESIGNER
Homeowners interested in upgrading the back or front door should consider investing in composite doors with their many benefits.
Below, we are going to explain more about composite doors, how they are made and discuss the benefits:

sections.heading: What Is A Composite Door?
body: A Composite door is a relatively new construction used in homes that has many advantages.
Composite doors have been designed to take into consideration flaws that are often common with singular material doors.
Composite is combining different materials, which can provide many benefits, making composite doors so effective.
One of the many advantages is resistant to weathering and not being affected by seasonal changes.
They also have high thermal resistance, something that wooden doors often do not have as there is no insulating foam inside the wooden door itself.

sections.heading: What Are Composite Doors Made Of And How Are They Made?
body: The syle of composite door determines the manufacturing process, but typically the following is the primary process:
The outside of a composite door is a 2mm layer of Glass Reinforced Plastic (GRP material), known as Fibreglass.

Fibreglass is used in the hull of boats as it can be easily moulded, is waterproof and extremely tough and durable. Fibreglass can also produce the wood effect, making the door look like a wooden door.
GRP panels are fused onto the UPVC internal door frame. Inside of that is a hardwood frame, creating a double frame effect, creating an extremely rigid and stable.

Thermal polyurethane foam is then injected and expands to fill all of the inner door space to provide excellent heat retaining insulation properties, increasing the doors energy efficiency. Alternatively, the door’s core can be made from solid timber.
The doors outer frame is made from a thick UPVC and steel reinforced to provide a very secure construction.
The door then goes through a manual process of fitting the windows and letterbox and any other door furniture.

sections.heading: The Benefits Of Composite Doors
body: Investing in composite doors does come with a lot of advantages. Here are some of the benefits and key features of buying composite doors.

sections.heading: Comparing Composite Doors To Wooden Doors
body: The first key benefit of investing in a composite door, instead of a wooden door, is that a composite door generally lasts longer and requires low maintenance than wooden doors.

Composite doors always maintain that new look, while wooden doors tend to look outdated, especially when the paint starts to dull or chip off, reducing wooden doors’ ability to withstand harsh weather conditions.
Moreover, when it comes to the pricing of these two products, composite doors are priced higher, but they are worth the extra investment.

sections.heading: The Best Front Door For Security
body: One thing is for sure, composite doors provide more safety and security than wooden doors. That is because composite doors have extra reinforced materials making them stronger and more durable. Composite doors are considered to be the most secure doors in the market.
Besides, being durable and robust, they also have a unique locking mechanism. These doors are designed to prevent unwanted intruders from accessing your home.

sections.heading: Doors With Style And Durability
body: As we now know, composite doors promote sustainability, are secure, and require low maintenance, the next thing to consider is style and durability.
Can we say that composite doors are durable and stylish?

Composite doors are available in a variety of styles and colours. These appearance options provide homeowners with an opportunity to customise their doors to suit their personal preferences and the look and feel of their homes.
Composite doors maintain their strength and longevity, along with providing great energy benefits.

sections.heading: Areas To Be Aware Of With Composite Doors
body: We’ve mentioned the many benefits of investing in composite doors, let’s touch on the areas to be aware of that need to be considered.

sections.heading: The Price Difference Between Composite Doors Compared To Other Doors
body: If you are on a budget, you need to be aware that a composite door is generally higher in price.

However, with all the benefits above, if you can stretch to buying composite doors, they really are an excellent investment in both looks, low maintenance, durability and security. You do get what you pay for.
If your budget is tight, or you prefer not to spend more than what you are willing to, you can consider investing in a UPVC door.

sections.heading: Do Composite Doors Fade Overtime?
body: As mentioned earlier, composite doors do not lose their look and only require little maintenance. That means you do not have to worry about your composite doors fading overtime.
The only time these doors can show fading signs is maybe after lasting for longer than they should, which composite doors can last up to thirty years.

sections.heading: How Long Will A Composite Door Last?
body: If taken good care of, a composite door can last for 30 years. That is the reason why these particular doors are popular and an excellent investment.

sections.heading: Is A Composite Door Better Than A Wooden Door?
body: After discussing both doors, we can clearly say yes, composite doors are much better than wooden doors. That is because they are durable, promote sustainability, and has customisable features.

sections.heading: Do Composite Doors Help To Keep The Warmth In The House?
body: Composite doors provide great energy benefits, which makes them great with promoting
energy efficiency
in the home. These doors are also 10% thicker compared to other doors that are sold in the market today.
Deciding on which door to buy is not easy. However, we hope this article has helped to answer any of your questions.
We believe you will make the right choice if you are happy to invest in the future and know what you want in design and style.

sections.heading: How Do You Maintain A Composite Door?
body: Keeping your door in the best possible condition is essential to maintain the door’s operation, but also, a clean front door makes the front of your home look clean.

sections.heading: Cleaning Your Composite Door
body: Door Leaf:

Clean using a warm soapy water solution and wipe off with a soft dry cloth. Do not want to use any abrasive cleaners or materials, or use high-pressure cleaners, steam cleaners, adhesives, solvents, and certainly not bleach.
Door Frame:
Using soapy water on the doorframe. To remove tough stains, use a PVCu cleaner while following the door manufacturers guidelines. Be sure not to use any abrasive materials.
External Glass:
Clean with warm soapy water to get most of the dirt off and wipe off with a soft cloth. Complete with a household glass cleaner. For leaded glass, you may notice oxidisation overtime.
Handle, Letter Plates, Numbers, Spy Holes, Door Knockers:
Clean with warm soapy solution with a touch of a very mild detergent to remove stubborn dirt.
Don’t use any solvents, abrasive products, and try to avoid scouring pads and metal polish on the door surface.
If there are rebates on the door, make sure they are dust-free and kept clean.

sections.heading: Composite Door Maintenance
body: Hinges:
Using engineering oil (preferably three and one) is the best way to lubricate every six months.
WD40 should be avoided to improve all of your moving parts, plus it dries out the surface very quickly when it comes into contact with them.
Locks:
Use a Teflon based lubricant every six months to keep the locks lubricated.
Weatherseal (Gasket):
When noticing the gaskets have come loose, slide them back into the available grooves. If they are broken or damaged, you need to contact us.

sections.heading: Why Choose A Composite Front Door?
body: The final decision to use a composite door is always going to be the choice of the homeowner.

It depends on what you would like to have as a front door to your house, or your back door to open up your home into your home, then start to look at all of your options, such as making a checklist, as to what you like and whether or not you can afford it.

Composite doors do provide so many advantages and benefits, such as being low maintenance. In most cases, these doors will go far beyond the life expectancy of a standard door, lasting 30 years or more.
Another benefit of these doors is having maximum energy efficiency to keep your home warm in the winter months.
Hopefully, we have answered many of the questions you have to help you decide how to move forward.

sections.heading: Consider Energy Efficient Windows For Your Home
body: ONLINE DESIGNER

sections.heading: What is an Energy-Efficient Window?
body: A typical home contains many windows and Windows are significant sources of energy loss in a house, with around 30 percent of your heating and cooling costs leaving through your windows.
With so much energy loss, even if you have central heating or air conditioning, you might still be paying more than you should be.
energy efficient window

works in four key areas. First, it minimizes the amount of escaping heat through the window. Second, it maximizes the amount of incoming solar radiation through the window. Third, it reduces glare. Finally, it makes the home more comfortable for occupants by blocking noise outside and insulating against cold air coming in.

sections.heading: How Do Energy Efficient Windows Work?
body: Energy-efficient window technology can convert solar energy into heating and cooling through advanced insulation. Window efficiency is determined by the U-factor, which measures heat flow. A higher U-factor indicates more heat will transfer through the window.

In summer, Energy efficient windows keep heat from coming in and heating your house during the day. In winter, they keep heat from escaping through the window glass and help lower your heating bills. An energy-efficient window works by using the sun’s natural power to provide light, reducing electricity use.

In the current economy, window efficiency is a serious concern for homeowners. To get the most energy-efficient windows, you need to measure your windows and determine what type of window is best for your needs. There are three ways to measure a window: by height, width, and area.

sections.heading: Window Energy Ratings: A, B, C Rated
body: A window with an A rating is more efficient than one with a B rating. A window with a C rating is less efficient than one with a B rating.
The Window energy rating is becoming more popular as properties need to be more environmentally friendly, and consumers want to save money on their energy bills.

Energy ratings are one of the most important aspects of window selection because they help you save money on your energy bills. Energy star rated windows can reduce your heating and cooling costs by up to 15%.

sections.heading: Why Should I Care About Energy Efficient Windows?
body: Some people might think there is no point in having energy-efficient windows because they cost more upfront and save money over the long term. There are many other reasons to get them that you should care about, such as:
Energy-efficient windows can help save money by lowering your heating and cooling bills.
When there’s a power outage, energy-efficient windows will keep out the cold or heat depending on the season.

Innovative windows are the newest trend in architecture, and they come with several benefits. Not only do you get to save energy with these windows, but you can also increase your security and comfort. If you’re on the hunt for new windows, consider buying those designed to be energy efficient.
New trends in architecture have begun to emerge as we try to find ways to use less natural resources and reduce our carbon footprint on the environment.

sections.heading: Single Glazing And Double Glazing For Energy Efficient Windows
body: The long-term energy savings that a single glazed window offers may not offset the higher purchase cost. In comparison, a double glazed window can provide up to eight times more insulation while using less energy, saving homeowners more money on their monthly utility bills.
Choosing double glazing or triple glazing will increase the energy efficiency of your replacement window, reducing heat loss in the winter month.

sections.heading: Our Final Words
body: Windows are used for ventilation, insulation, and light. All these functions are essential to human life, but they also impact the environment. That’s why
energy efficient windows
are a significant contribution to green construction around the world.

Energy efficiency is not the only determinant in its life span, but it is an essential factor. Windows can serve many purposes, and there are many different types and models. The most significant difference between
windows for your home
is that some offer better energy efficiency than others.
To know more about our energy efficient windows,
get in touch with our team

sections.heading: Introduction
body: This Cookie Policy refers to cookies used in websites operated by Fenster Glazing & Locks Ltd.

sections.heading: What Are Cookies?
body: Cookies are tiny files that are downloaded to your computer, to improve your experience when using a website. As is common practice with almost all professional websites this site uses cookies. This page describes what information they gather, how we use it and why we sometimes need to store these cookies.

sections.heading: Disabling Cookies
body: You can prevent the setting of cookies by adjusting the settings on your browser (see your browser Help for how to do this). Be aware that disabling cookies will affect the functionality of this and many other websites that you visit. Disabling cookies will usually result in also disabling certain functionality and features of this site. Therefore, it is recommended that you do not disable cookies.

sections.heading: The Cookies We Set
body: There may be the capability to create an account on this website. If you create an account with us then we will use cookies for the management of the signup process and general administration. These cookies will usually be deleted when you log out however in some cases they may remain afterwards to remember your site preferences when logged out.

We use cookies when you are logged in so that we can remember this fact. This prevents you from having to log in every single time you visit a new page. These cookies are typically removed or cleared when you log out to ensure that you can only access restricted features and areas when logged in.

This site offers newsletter or email subscription services and cookies may be used to remember if you are already registered and whether to show certain notifications which might only be valid to subscribed/unsubscribed users.

From time to time we offer user surveys and questionnaires to provide you with interesting insights, helpful tools, or to understand our user base more accurately. These surveys may use cookies to remember who has already taken part in a survey or to provide you with accurate results after you change pages.

sections.heading: Third Party Cookies and Remarketing
body: In some special cases we also use cookies provided by trusted third parties. The following section details some common third party cookies you might encounter through this site.

Google Analytics: Our website uses Google Analytics, one of the most popular and trusted analytics solutions, to help us to understand how people use our website. It does this by tracking such information as how long people spend on our website, the pages they visit, the website that referred them to our website and other aggregate data. We do this so that we can make improvements to our website and provide a better user experience and more engaging content.

Google AdWords: We may use Google AdWords remarketing which allows us to reach people who have been on our website, and show them adverts relevant to the pages they have visited. This means, after your visit to our website, you may be shown ads by Google either within the Google Display Network or Google search results. Google AdWords uses cookies in order to show ads based on your past visits to websites to provide relevant ads for products and services of interest to you.
You can adjust your settings and also opt out of Google’s use of AdWords cookies by visiting
Google’s Ads Settings.

Google AdSense: We may use the Google AdSense service to serve advertising. The Google AdSense service uses a DoubleClick cookie to serve more relevant ads across the web and limit the number of times that a given ad is shown to you. You can adjust your settings and also opt out of Google’s use of AdSense cookies by visiting
Google’s Ads Settings

Facebook Pixel: This involves incorporating a tracking pixel (Facebook Pixel) in the head section of our website, which marks website visitors and recognises them the next time they visit the social network. The pixel uses browser information, visited websites and a hashed Facebook ID of the website user. This makes it possible for us to employ retargeting, i.e. to show you relevant Facebook ads about products or services of interest to you.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
body: Our staff, based in Milton Keynes, welcome questions from our clients. To make the process easier, we have compiled a list of the most common questions. If you still need more information, feel free to get in touch with us online or over the phone.

sections.heading: What accreditation do you have?
body: Fenster Glazing are fully accredited by FENSA, the leading government-authorised competent persons scheme for the window and door industry in the UK. This means every double glazing installation we complete – including uPVC windows, aluminium bifold doors and composite front doors – meets or exceeds Building Regulations for energy efficiency and safety.

sections.heading: What’s the best way to find prices?
body: The fastest way to get a price for your new windows and doors is through our Instant Pricing Tool online. Whether you’re looking for energy-efficient uPVC casement windows, ultra-slim aluminium bifold doors, or secure composite entrance doors, you can also speak directly to our expert sales team by phone or email for a fast, practical quote.

sections.heading: Do you provide a guarantee?
body: Yes – Fenster Glazing provides a 10-year insurance-backed guarantee on every window and door installation. Whether it’s double glazed uPVC windows, aluminium bifolding doors or replacement composite doors, our guarantee ensures long-lasting performance and total peace of mind.

sections.heading: Do you use your own installers?
body: Absolutely. All our installations are carried out by our in-house team of expert window and door fitters based in Milton Keynes. Every installer is trained to handle uPVC, aluminium and composite systems, ensuring the highest standards of workmanship, compliance, and customer satisfaction.

sections.heading: Deal With Condensation On Double Glazed Windows
body: ONLINE DESIGNER

sections.heading: Condensation in the UK
body: As the winter settles into full swing, more and more households are complaining about the presence of condensation on their
windows
. In fact, at the start of December 2022, it was reported that 1 in 5 households in the UK experienced issues with condensation.

There are several frequently stated tips for reducing the amount of condensation present on your windows, most of which involve keeping the temperature of your home warm, or opening the windows for effective ventilation.
But with the ongoing cost of living crisis, and some of the coldest weather Britain has experienced in years, this may just not be feasible for a large percentage of the population.

In 2021, it was estimated that 30% of heating costs were a result of heat escaping via your windows. Coupled with the 6.5% energy bill increase in October 2022, it is not surprising that most households aren’t willing to keep windows open and consistently have the heating on.
So what can we do to reduce the amount of condensation on double glazed windows which isn’t going to break the bank?

sections.heading: What is condensation?
body: When it comes to double glazing, there are three different types of condensation; exterior, interior and internal.

Exterior condensation refers to condensation which appears on the outside of the window. Despite popular belief, this type of condensation is positive and is an indicator that your double glazed windows are performing as they should.
When the droplets form on the outside of the window, it is a clear indication that the warm air from your home is remaining on the inside of your home, whilst cooler air is being kept out.

sections.heading: Why do you get condensation on the inside of double glazed windows
body: Unfortunately, unlike exterior condensation, interior and internal condensation are not so favourable.

Interior condensation occurs when the warm air of your home meets the cool surface of your window. It indicates that the air within your home is high in humidity and if untreated, it can lead to black mould which can be detrimental to your health.

Internal condensation is by far the most serious of the three and is caused as a result of the seal between your glass panes being broken. Unfortunately, this means your windows are underperforming. It is not easily fixed and therefore, is likely to require you to install new windows.
As a result, the rest of this article will be focused on interior condensation.

sections.heading: How to stop interior condensation on double glazed windows
body: As discussed, the most effective way to reduce condensation on the interior of your double glazed windows is to increase ventilation and keep the temperature of your home as consistent as possible.

It is worth noting, that this doesn’t require your heating to be on full all of the time, but just to be present in the background. However, with so many struggling to meet their monthly bills as it is, let’s consider some more cost effective solutions.
Here are 4 easy to follow, practically free, tips…

sections.heading: Dry clothes outside
body: As clothes dry the water droplets in them vaporise and increase the humidity of the air in your home. By drying them outside, you are reducing the humidity of the air in your household which can contribute to condensation.

With the Great British weather being the way it is, it is understandable that this isn’t always feasible. Therefore, in such instances, it is recommended that clothing is dried in a ventilated room such as a bathroom with an extractor fan.
Always avoid drying clothes over the radiator as this simply speeds up the vaporisation process and leads to increased volumes of condensation.

sections.heading: Use pan lids when cooking
body: Using pan lids when cooking can be a great way of reducing the amount of humidity present within your home.
When boiling any form of liquid, a certain amount evaporates into the air, contributing to the overall humidity of your home, therefore, increasing the likelihood of condensation.
Using pan lids is also a great way for saving on your energy bills as liquids warm quicker and therefore, less energy is required for cooking.

sections.heading: Review the location of fish tanks and plants
body: Plants are great for improving the air quality of your home and fish are a very common house pet across the UK. However, the placement of both of these could be contributing towards the condensation on your double glazing.

Both give off water vapour which, if met with the right surface such as a window, will condense. When placed next to a window, sunlight can increase the speed at which water vapour is given off, meaning that it is accelerating the speed at which condensation can be produced.

In such instances, it is recommended that, where possible, plants are kept outdoors during the winter months, or away from the window where possible. With regards to fish tanks, again these should be kept away from windows and ideally close to a well ventilated room, such as a kitchen with an extractor fan.

sections.heading: Keep bathroom and kitchen doors closed
body: It will come at no surprise that the kitchen and bathroom are the two rooms in the house most likely to contribute towards condensation on your double glazing.
Keeping the door closed on these rooms whilst in use can significantly help reduce the amount of condensation present on your double glazing windows.

Most kitchens and bathrooms have adequate ventilation to make them fit for purpose, therefore, using these facilities, such as an extractor fan, can help ensure that any humidity produced is not circulated elsewhere in the house.

For households which do not have adequate ventilation, it is recommended to buy a dehumidifier for these rooms. The dehumidifier will not be required to be in constant use, and by closing the door, can ensure that it is only filtering the air from that one particular room.
There are many energy efficient dehumidifiers available on the market.

sections.heading: Say goodbye to condensation
body: Whilst the presence of condensation on your double glazing can be a nuisance, if untreated it can become very detrimental to the health of both your windows and household occupants.
But the good news is, there are some simple, cheap steps you can take to help reduce the damage at hand. So use these tips and start making your home a condensation free zone!

sections.heading: Difference Between French Doors and Sliding Patio Doors?
body: ONLINE DESIGNER
There are many things to consider when looking to purchase
French doors
patio
bi-fold doors
with many differences, constraints and designs.
Patio doors, also referred to as sliding doors, have morphed over time and now encompass different doors styles leading out to the garden or outside patio areas.
The different patio doors may fold or slide and may even open just like your front or back door.

We understand that it’s all very confusing, so we’ve written this article to help ease your decision and help you to understand the differences between ‘French doors’ and ‘Sliding doors’ for your patio area for your home.

sections.heading: What Is The Difference? And, Which One Is Best Suited To My Needs?
body: Both French and sliding doors will come in a wide array of sizes. However, you need to be aware of the differences to consider before you buy your door:
French doors are by tradition hung on hinges. They are double doors and typically open outwardly. However, there are a few instances in which they will open inwardly.

When the doors are open, you’ll have full access to the width of the doorway. However, you main be constrained by the maximum leaf size, which means you’ll have less space when you open the doors. The maximum opening width for French doors is typically 1800 mm wide.
With smaller-sized french doors, you have full-width access that’s ideal for smaller apartments or homes, or small garden spaces also utilize narrower sizes.

sections.heading: Sliding Patio Doors
body: The sliding patio doors allow for a more expansive opening space as they are all standard sized at 1600mm to 4200 mm.
The only issue is that only 50 percent of the space can be used at a time. When the doors are opened wide, there is still half the door that isn’t usable, reducing the garden’s opening space.
Sliding doors are ideal if you have a restricted space. They don’t require space to open inward or outward, and they only slide open or closed, making them perfect for smaller spaces.
Over the previous years, the sliding patio doors have significantly declined in popularity. More people have gone to folding doors (Bi-fold doors) or French doors that open the opening’s full width.

sections.heading: So Which Doors Should You Choose?
body: French doors or sliding doors are a huge decision. There is much to consider when determining which will work best for your needs.

sections.heading: The Cost
body: While the different styles’ cost will vary depending upon the opening’s size, you’ll want to consider the price per square meter for the doors opening.
Sliding doors are typically 10 to 20 percent cheaper when you select a size that is over 1800 mm.
The locking mechanisms and the hardware are typically sold with the door, making them far more cost-effective than French doors.
For sizes over 1800 mm, French doors may become more restrictive in price as they will require specific additional hardware, such as requiring more windows and sidelights.

sections.heading: Your Homes Security
body: While all of the options come with their unique security features, you must consider some essential factors before buying.

sections.heading: Sliding Patio Doors
body: Ensure that your doors have the following:
Multi-point locks
Security hooks that keep the doors from being levered open
Drop bolts that lock
Anti lift devices
Anti bump and lockable cylinders to keep the door barrel from being forced
Double glazing with the Secure by Design approval to ensure that they were tested and approved by the Association of Chief Police Officer.
Take these into consideration:
Multi-point locks are a must-have for French doors. These should be 3 or 5 point locks and lock into the frame.
French doors should have a cover spline to ensure there is no gap between the doors where they meet together.

sections.heading: Performance
body: Ensure the doors have the proper thermal efficiency or the U value. The lower the U value, the better performance. Part L will cover this for Building Regulations.
You’ll have to ensure that the doors are double glazed and have toughened glass, compliant with BSE 12150, for safety and security.
You’ll want to consider all ventilation requirements for the property as well as what the products offer. You’ll need to be compliant with Part F for the UK Building Regulations.
When comparing the door types, remember these things:
Consider the size of your opening.
Consider your cost.
Consider performance and thermal loss or gain.
Consider ventilation requirements.
Consider the security of the door.
Consider your budget.

sections.heading: Different Types Of Window Frame Materials
body: ONLINE DESIGNER
This article looks at the different types of materials used for window frames and each material’s advantages and disadvantages.

sections.heading: Wooden Timber Window Frames
body: While this is the most classic look, it is also going to be the most expensive. Also, it provides a low thermal conductivity, which means heat doesn’t easily pass through the window frame.
Wooden Timber is one of the best forms of material when considering energy efficiency. Wooden Timber is a natural insulator and helps to absorb and retain heat.
Wooden Timber also tends to be the most attractive. However, this material will require more maintenance due to it being a natural material.
Wooden frames can be constructed from both Hardwood and softwood.
Softwood
Timber is renewable, but frame performance, maintenance, lifespan and finish all depend on the species, treatment and installation quality.
Hardwood
grows much slower and is quite durable, leading to a higher price.
Modern wood frames are designed to be strong, meaning they will not bow or warp and have been treated to withstand fungus and rot.

In addition to the natural beauty of wood, it can also be painted or stained. Wood is the only frame material on this list that can be painted numerous times, allowing you to customise your home’s look.

sections.heading: Advantages Of Wooden Window Frames:
body: Wood tends to fit perfectly on a period property while being a stipulation through building regulations.
Wood adds a sense of style and grace to your home.
If the wood is treated correctly and maintained, it can last considerably longer than PVC.

sections.heading: Disadvantages Of Wooden Window Frames:
body: Wood is considerably more expensive than cheaper PVC windows.
Your Windows will need a fair amount of work and regular maintenance to ensure they stay in good condition.

Wood is prone to rotting and warping, causing gaps in the window seal. This can increase draft and noise into the home, increase your home’s heating costs, cause difficulties opening and closing the windows and reduce the security of your home.

sections.heading: UPVC Window Frames
body: Affordably priced and long-lasting, these low maintenance window frames are a good option.

UPVC has been regarded as an almost miracle material that has made it a go-to source for many projects. The truth is UPVC is an excellent material that is not going to rust, flake or rot. Additionally, UPVC is one of the best for energy efficiency that offers double glazing and can achieve an A+12 Window Energy Rating.
UPVC is a highly popular option for windows because it offers such good value for the money. However, it does not hold the same style and charm as other materials.
It is possible to purchase UPVC that resembles a traditional timber frame. In fact, it is rather difficult to tell the difference.
In the past, if you had windows, they were white. However, UPVC has changed all of that, offering a rainbow of colours that will last a lifetime without the need to repaint.
In addition, a significant number of windows now contain lead-free UPVC, which was a health issue.

sections.heading: Advantages Of UPVC Window Frames
body: Typically, one of the cheapest options available.
There is very little maintenance associated with UPVC.
Even though it is one of the cheapest materials, it still offers good thermal performance.

sections.heading: Disadvantages Of UPVC Window Frames
body: Can be rather difficult to repair.
UPVC, especially white UPVC, can discolour with time due to exposure to the sun. However, discolouring is minimal these days using a high-quality UPVC window frame.

UPVC has been difficult to recycle and not environmentally friendly. However, using high-quality UPVC is recyclable and is environmentally sustainable, therefore it’s important to find a Glazing company that supplies high-quality recyclable UPVC window frames.
UPVC has a shorter lifespan as opposed to other window frames.

sections.heading: Aluminium & Steel Window Frames
body: Aluminium and Steel Windows are slimmer frames that allow the most amount of sunlight into the home. They are highly stylish, making them perfect for the contemporary building.

Aluminium frames are typically used in structural glazing in a variety of commercial projects due to their strength. The strength allows the window frame to be much thinner with a larger glass surface, enabling increased light levels into a room.
Aluminium is known as a natural conductor of heat, which allows heat to pass through easily.
Aluminium window frames

contain a thermal barrier that helps in the reduction of heat loss. Over the past ten years, thermal barrier technology has dramatically improved, and an aluminium window has the same performance as a UPVC window.
Aluminium frames also require very little maintenance and are highly weatherproof. Unlike some other metals, aluminium will not corrode, meaning your windows are not going to rust or flake.
In the past, if you wanted aluminium window frames, you had to settle for silver as your colour of choice. That has changed as now you have a wide range of colours available to match your home.

sections.heading: Advantages Of Metal Window Frames:
body: Durable and long-lasting frames.
Easy to recycle and reuse in many instances.

sections.heading: Disadvantages Of Metal Window Frames:
body: While metal frames can be recycled, there is considerable CO2 produced in making these types of frames, in addition to a much longer form of embodied energy.
Metal frames do require regular maintenance to protect them from corrosion.
Lower thermal performance as opposed to UPVC.

sections.heading: Composite Window Frames
body: Composite window frames take two elements and offer the benefits of many different materials: increasing energy efficiency, security, lifespan and better aesthetics.
There are some composites which make use of an aluminium-clad timber, which offers incredible insulation and weatherproofing. There are some composite windows which feature a UPVC core.

sections.heading: Advantages Of Composite Window Frames:
body: Longer lasting.
Offers premium insulation.
Save on energy.
Reliable and robust.
Very low maintenance.

sections.heading: Disadvantages Of Composite Window Frames:
body: One of the only downsides to a composite material window is the cost. They are at the top of the price ladder, making them not as affordable as a uPVC window.
There are many advantages and disadvantages of the materials used in window frames, each working for your needs and requirements.

sections.heading: Composite, uPVC & Aluminium Door Maintenance
body: Doors are your home's first chance at a good impression. Make sure your doors stay clean and presentable with our expert cleaning and maintenance tips.

sections.heading: Door Maintenance Guide
body: With service areas including Milton Keynes, Northampton, Ampthill, Toddington, Leighton Buzzard, Buckinghamshire, and the neighbouring Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire regions, Fenster Glazing is proud to offer high-quality door installations throughout the Midlands.

Composite, uPVC & Aluminium Doors are exposed to environmental factors like wind, rain, and pollution, which can cause dirt to build up. Fenster doors can withstand dirt, but it is still advisable to clean them frequently to keep them looking good.

sections.heading: Cleaning Frequency:
body: We know that door maintenance can be tough for homeowners with busy lifestyles. However, routine is key, especially for door maintenance! In urban or coastal areas, clean the doors every three months; however, in rural areas, a biannual cleaning schedule should suffice. By periodically cleaning your doors, you will prevent them from being damaged in the long term and keep them looking fresh.

sections.heading: General Cleaning:
body: For general door maintenance, you won’t need to buy any extra products, making it one step easier for you. Wipe away with a soft cloth and a mild soap or washing-up liquid solution to perform general cleaning. This is to wipe away dirt or dust. To tackle grease marks, apply a small quantity of washing-up liquid without water, followed by a rinse with clean water. Avoid the use of glass cleaners as well as kitchen or bathroom cleaners during your door maintenance.

sections.heading: Tough Stains:
body: For neglected uPVC surfaces, employ a specialised uPVC cream cleaner to clean the areas.

To address long-neglected aluminium doors, use washing-up liquid with minimal water. Scrub the surface vigorously with a stiff fibre brush, then rinse thoroughly with clean water. Just take simple door maintenance steps to keep your door looking clean again. Please don’t use alternative cleaning agents, caustic or ammonia-based products, scouring powder, or abrasive cleaners, including steel wool or scouring pads. Stick to our steps, and your door maintenance will be hassle-free!

sections.heading: Post-Maintenance Instructions for Composite, uPVC & Aluminium Doors
body: Composite, uPVC & Aluminium Doors are exposed to environmental factors like wind, rain, and pollution, which can cause dirt to build up. Fenster doors can withstand dirt, but it is still advisable to clean them frequently to keep them looking good.
To make your door maintenance routine efficient, we recommend the following our comprehensive door maintenance guide.

sections.heading: Standard Glass Maintenance
body: The door maintenance for standard glass also has simple steps to keep it clean. For routine cleaning, employ a soft cloth and a mild soap or washing-up liquid solution to wipe away the surfaces.

Tougher stains can make door maintenance hard, but luckily, we only recommend two simple steps to look after your door. Use a commercial window cleaning solution or cream and follow the provided instructions to clean off stubborn stains. Be careful that the solution does not come into contact with the door frame to avoid damaging it. Rinse the glass thoroughly with clean water to eliminate any residue. Please refrain from using creams containing abrasive pastes, steel wool, or razor blades for the removal of stubborn marks.

If you have leaded glass in your door, maintaning it is a bit different than traditional glass. Over time, the lead used in leaded glass undergoes natural weathering, resulting in a uniformly oxidised appearance.

The duration of this process may vary depending on the level of exposure to the elements and the specific location (urban or rural). We recommend exercising patience and allowing this natural course to unfold.

sections.heading: Cleaning Door Accessories
body: In your door maintenance routine, it’s important to remember to look after your accessories too. When cleaning your door accessories, use these simple steps to look after them. For regular cleaning, use a soft cloth and a mild soap or washing-up liquid solution to get rid of easy marks. When addressing stainless steel or letterboxes, remove surface dirt by gently dusting with a soft cloth.

While doing door maintenance, look after the stubborn stains by using white spirit or a high-quality, non-abrasive car wax polish. Avoid using alternative cleaning agents, metal cleaners, caustic or ammonia-based products, scouring powder, steel wool, or scouring pads.

sections.heading: Lock and Hinge Maintenance
body: It’s important to maintain the locks on your door. After cleaning, it is important to lubricate the locks so they can last longer. Lubricate locks exclusively with light machine oil and refrain from using alternative oils, grease, or WD40 while doing door maintenance.

Ensure you have a spare key readily available, preferably entrusted to a dependable neighbour. Please note that removing a lock from a door without a key is not feasible. For all access and security emergencies, please contact our office at 01908 429200.

For hinges, apply light machine oil as necessary to lubricate catches, restrictors, and window hinges. We advise against using any other type of oil or grease. Also, don’t lubricate plastic moving parts during your door maintenance, as they possess self-lubricating properties.

sections.heading: Casement Windows Dunstable
body: Casement windows will genuinely improve any home, and their performance and quality look have been proven to be of a high standard. They keep your home warm without the need for more heating systems and, in doing so, improve your carbon efficiency.

sections.heading: Weatherproof Windows
body: Your windows need to withstand any weather conditions the UK has to offer, and our
casement windows

offer just that. These windows are designed to offer fantastic levels of weatherproofing and protection from all of the elements. When closed, the sash goes tightly against the frame to keep the wind and rain out of your home, keeping you warm and dry.

sections.heading: Slim Sightlines
body: The ultraslim sightlines are the thin frames that the casement windows have, a particular feature that allows for a larger pane of glass. The advantages of having slim sightlines are that they provide you with unobstructed views of the outside world and allow natural light to shine into your home. In doing so, they create a welcoming space in your home and allow you to enjoy the outside from the comfort of your Dunstable home.

sections.heading: Low Maintenance
body: A true advantage of having casement windows installed is that they are very low in maintenance and are very simple to clean. Once the casement windows are in place, there is no need for repainting or resanding, as these uPVC windows have superior protection against the elements. In order to maintain their beautiful look, all you will need to do is a mere, occasional wipedown with warm, soapy water. So you can sit back and enjoy the views with the constant need to upkeep the casement windows.

sections.heading: Ultimate Security
body: Security is forever the most important element of any window, and your family should always feel safe in your home. Because of their design, our casement windows offer quality security features which reduce the risk of forced entry to an absolute minimum. Our uPVC casement windows have excellent durability and reinforced glass to keep your home safe and sound. At

, we have a selection of anti-burglar handles that deliver protection from any intruders even further. Casement windows are also family-friendly as they are simple to open and close, an ideal feature for families with children or elderly people.

sections.heading: Noise Reduction
body: Due to uPVC casement windows’ thermal insulation, your home will be superior at reducing noise from the outside. Noise pollution, such as the sounds of traffic or noisy neighbours, will lessen at an impressive rate, as casement windows can be an effective barrier against outdoor noise. You and your family will be able to enjoy a more relaxing home environment.

sections.heading: Energy Efficient Windows
body: Each of our double-glazing casement windows has an A+ energy rating, which is the highest energy-efficient rating that can be found anywhere on the market. The energy rating proves that our casement windows are incredibly effective at preventing heat loss in your home, keeping the warm air in. The exceptional thermal performance means you can also benefit from lower energy bills and improve your carbon footprint as you will be less dependent on central heating.

sections.heading: Stunning Look
body: Casement windows have a timeless look that can suit any home, whether modern or contemporary, bringing with it a charming and effective style. The slim sightlines are sleek and give your home a fresh, new look on the outside while improving your the inside with bright, natural light. By choosing Fenster Glazing, we have a stunning range of customisation options to choose from so you can have the casement windows you are looking for. A selection of colour options means you can have casement windows that could make your Dunstable home stand out or match the decor effortlessly. From classic white casement windows to chartwell green casement windows, you can find the option you want. Our glass options can further add character to your home and a style that is truly bespoke to you.

sections.heading: What energy ratings come with your windows and doors?

sections.heading: Do you dispose of the old windows and doors?

sections.heading: Why We Follow Glass and Glazing Federation (GGF) Standards at Fenster Glazing
body: Understanding Quality and Clarity in Your Double Glazed Windows and Doors

When investing in new double glazed windows or doors, clarity, quality and performance are understandably top priorities. But what does “high quality glazing” actually mean? How do you know if what you’re getting meets industry standards?

At Fenster Glazing, we believe in full transparency. That is why we follow guidance from the Glass and Glazing Federation, alongside the relevant Building Regulations and manufacturer installation requirements.
Glass and Glazing Federation (GGF)
– the recognised voice of the UK’s glazing industry.

sections.heading: What Is the Glass and Glazing Federation?
body: The GGF is the leading authority for companies involved in glass manufacture, processing, supply and installation. Their guidance sets out consistent, professional standards across the glazing industry, ensuring customers receive products and services they can trust.
Their
“Quality of Vision”
document is one of the most important guidelines we follow at Fenster Glazing.

sections.heading: What Does “Quality of Vision” Mean?
body: When viewing new windows or doors, particularly in bright light, you might notice minor imperfections in the glass, such as small blemishes, bubbles, or slight distortions. This is completely normal and, in most cases, expected.
The GGF’s
“Quality of Vision” standard
exists to define what is considered acceptable in double glazed units. It helps homeowners and installers alike understand the natural variations in glass and avoid unnecessary concerns.
In short, it separates cosmetic, unavoidable features from genuine defects.

sections.heading: Our Commitment to GGF Standards
body: At Fenster Glazing, we take pride in doing things properly. That means using top-quality materials, fitting them with precision, and ensuring everything meets the latest industry standards. One of the most important frameworks we follow is the guidance set out by the
Glass and Glazing Federation (GGF)

The GGF sets clear, nationally recognised standards for the visual quality and performance of glass used in windows and doors. These guidelines are designed to protect homeowners and make sure everyone knows what to expect from modern double and triple glazed units.

sections.heading: What Do GGF Standards Actually Cover?
body: In simple terms, the GGF guidelines help define what counts as acceptable in terms of how your sealed units should look and perform. They acknowledge that no glass is completely flawless, but there are very clear rules on what is and isn’t considered acceptable.
Here’s how we apply those principles at Fenster.

sections.heading: How Glass Is Professionally Inspected
body: When a sealed unit is inspected, it isn’t about putting your nose to the glass and hunting for specks. A proper inspection is done in natural daylight, by standing directly in front of the unit and looking through the glass (not at it).
Stand at least
2 metres away
For toughened, laminated or coated glass, spacer and edge-cover requirements are checked against the relevant specification before the unit is ordered.
3 metres
The check is done at a
90-degree angle
, not from the side
The
outer 50mm edge

sections.heading: What Counts as Normal in Sealed Units?
body: Glass used in sealed units is processed to a high standard, but like any manufactured material, very minor imperfections can occur. These are considered acceptable if they are small and not grouped together.
Here’s what you might see from time to time, especially when viewed in the right lighting:
Tiny
bubbles or blisters
Fine scratches
under 25mm in length
Minute particles
inside the sealed unit
These features do not affect the performance of your windows. They’re part of how glass is made and are recognised within the GGF’s official quality tolerance.

sections.heading: Special Glass Types: What to Know
body: Certain types of high-performance glass may behave a little differently visually:
Toughened glass
can show slight optical distortion due to the way it’s heat treated
Laminated glass
may contain minor blemishes due to its layered construction
Low-E (low-emissivity) coatings
can appear slightly hazy or create a gentle film effect in some lighting
These are natural effects and are not faults. They simply come with the advanced performance benefits these glass types offer.

sections.heading: Common Optical Effects
body: Occasionally you might notice visual effects that can occur even in premium sealed units:
Condensation
can still happen in specific weather or humidity conditions
Multiple reflections
are caused by light bouncing between the layers of glass
Brewster’s fringes
(subtle rainbow effects) are a natural result of light passing through parallel glass surfaces
These effects are completely normal and part of how modern glazing behaves.

sections.heading: Why GGF Standards Matter to You
body: Your sealed units meet the UK’s trusted benchmarks for clarity and performance
Every installation is checked using the correct method
You get a fair understanding of what to expect from your new windows
We also provide a
10-year guarantee
on our installations and only use glass that meets or exceeds the GGF’s visual quality standards. It’s part of our promise to deliver a better experience from quote to completion.
If you want to check the source guidance, visit the Glass and Glazing Federation website or ask Fenster to talk you through the relevant standard for your project.
